query:
The group decided to order pizza. What did Soo-Yeon's response to that decision reveal about her actual position, and what specifically in how she responded signals this — given that she did not object?

Options:
A. Soo-Yeon
B. Nadia
C. Lena
D. Kezia
context:
[1] (about=Soo-Yeon, episodic, t4 @2026-03-09T19:26:00) Priya mentioned pizza for tonight. Can we do something lighter? I had a heavy lunch 😅
[2] (about=Lena, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:13:00) so basically Soo-Yeon ran a successful theory of mind intervention tbh. she identified the barrier and reframed the proposition. elegant
[3] (about=Soo-Yeon, episodic, t4 @2026-03-09T19:13:00) she has good taste in groups 🙂
[4] (about=Kezia, episodic, t6 @2026-03-16T19:19:00) fine with pizza 🍕
[5] (about=Priya, episodic, t6 @2026-03-16T19:21:00) lol ok pizza it is i guess 😅 majority wins. Nadia you want in on the order?
[6] (about=Soo-Yeon, core, t4 @2026-03-09T19:01:00) Requests lighter food than pizza for tonight due to a heavy lunch.
[7] (about=Soo-Yeon, core, t4 @2026-03-09T19:01:00) Compliments Kezia's taste in groups.
[8] (about=GROUP, said_by=Priya, group-interaction, t6 @2026-03-16T19:01:00) Group decides to order pizza for the session, with majority vote; Nadia opts out.
[9] (about=GROUP, said_by=Priya, group-interaction, t4 @2026-03-09T19:01:00) Tonight's snack changed from pizza to lighter options: rice crackers, hummus, and mixed nuts.
agent_answer:
**A. Soo-Yeon**

Soo-Yeon’s actual position was that she **did not want pizza**; she preferred something **lighter** because she’d had a heavy lunch.  

The signal is in how she framed it: she didn’t directly object to pizza, but asked, **“Can we do something lighter? I had a heavy lunch 😅”** — a soft request/question and a reframe rather than an outright no. That reveals her real preference while avoiding direct confrontation.

query:
The group discussed the expectation that everyone should bring either a game or food to the annual marathon. What did Nadia's response signal about her actual relationship to this group norm, and how would you know from what she said?

Options:
A. Nadia
B. Tomasz
C. Marcus
D. Lena
context:
[1] (about=Nadia, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:06:00) I will bring a game. I do not participate in the food arrangement.
[2] (about=Tomasz, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:04:00) In my experience the marathon only works when everyone contributes. It is the social contract of a shared day.
[3] (about=Priya, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:07:00) that totally counts Nadia! honestly a good game pitch is worth more than another bag of chips 😊
[4] (about=Lena, episodic, t12 @2026-04-13T19:10:00) so basically that explains why Nadia didn't push back on Tomasz's Dune ruling even though everyone else was complaining tbh
[5] (about=Nadia, episodic, t12 @2026-04-13T19:38:00) I did not want to interrupt the game.
[6] (about=Nadia, core, t12 @2026-04-13T19:01:00) Explains she did not want to interrupt the game, hence not mentioning the food issue.
[7] (about=Nadia, core, t14 @2026-04-20T19:01:00) Will bring a game to the marathon but does not participate in food arrangement.
agent_answer:
**A. Nadia**

Nadia’s response signals **partial/qualified compliance** with the group norm: she was willing to contribute by **bringing a game**, but she explicitly **opted out of the food arrangement**. In other words, she accepted the “game or food” expectation in the game form, while refusing the food side of it.

We know this from her own words: **“I will bring a game. I do not participate in the food arrangement.”** The memory also records that she **will bring a game to the marathon but does not participate in food arrangement**, and that she explained she **did not want to interrupt the game**.
